transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-10-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (CTO), Priya (ML), Tom (Infra), Mark (Security), Samir (SRE), Kelsey (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quasar is building a real-time doc summarization/chat product for enterprise customers; primary constraints are p95 latency under ~300ms for short interactive queries, plus ability to handle steady-state concurrency of ~120 streams and token peaks of ~8k-16k tokens/sec. They are evaluating Hosted to move fast but have strong interest in Dedicated or Private due to PHI and residency.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? i'm Maya, AE on Redwood inference.
[00:00:08] Lena: hi, lena here, CTO at Quasar. we're trying to figure out how to serve streaming summaries for our enterprise product.
[00:00:12] Tom: tom, infra. we care about tail latency and how that impacts UX.
[00:00:16] Priya: priya, ML lead, will own the prompt set and evals.
[00:00:20] Diego: diego, solutions engineer, i'll walk through some performance patterns later.
[00:00:27] Mark: mark, security. i'll ask about KMS, audit logs and on-prem options.
[00:00:32] Maya: great. quick agenda — p95 and concurrency targets, current architecture, and we can map hosting options and next steps. sound good?
[00:00:38] Lena: yep. we'll start with our targets — we want interactive summaries where the UI streams partial text; goal is p95 under 300ms for typical 16-64 token responses, but we also need to handle longer completions up to 512 tokens for full-document summaries.
[00:00:55] Priya: to add, our median is usually 40 tokens for chat, but for summarization endpoints we can get 200-500 tokens. typical user flow is: upload document, model produces condensed highlights + interactive clarifications.
[00:01:06] Diego: got it. so two profiles — streaming short chat with tight p95, and batchy long summaries where throughput matters. how many concurrent users are you expecting?
[00:01:16] Lena: during peak, about 5k active users which translates roughly to 100-140 concurrent streaming sessions hitting inference.
[00:01:24] Samir: and we see token peaks when large documents are summarized — bursts that can push token/sec to 8k-16k for a minute or two.
[00:01:33] Maya: that's helpful. on the latency side, what SLO do you need for the core UX? p95 300ms across regions, or is region-bound?
[00:01:42] Tom: US-east is primary; p95 300ms is target for US-east. EU is lower priority but still important.
[00:01:50] Diego: ok. quick note — streaming p95 at 300ms for small tokens often depends on prefix cache, KV cache hit rates, and batching window. if you disable batching for single-turn low-latency, cost goes up.
[00:02:04] Priya: we care about cost too; we can't double our inference spend. so cost/latency tradeoffs are key.
[00:02:09] Maya: understood. i'd like to outline hosting options — hosted API is fastest to get started with, Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you control for PHI. each has different latency and cost profiles.
[00:02:23] Mark: can you run through security differences quickly? we need SOC2, audit logs, KMS/HSM support, and SSO/SAML.
[00:02:30] Diego: yes — we have SOC2 docs, audit logs in Redwood Console, and we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS in many cases as well. i'll share exact links.
[00:02:43] Kelsey: what's the friction to move from Hosted to Dedicated when we grow?
[00:02:47] Maya: you can start on Hosted and then reserve Dedicated capacity — we have migration guides and model pinning so you won't have to change prompts. turnaround for Dedicated setup is typically a few weeks depending on committed config.
[00:02:58] Lena: what about cold-starts and warm KV cache for streaming? large docs will often hit cold KV cache.
[00:03:06] Diego: good point — KV cache helps for multi-turn dialogues. for single-document summarization, prefix caching and pre-populating KV entries during ingest can reduce first-token latency. for large doc summarization, you may still see higher p95 — that's where dedicated capacity with pinned model weights helps because it reduces paging and quantization overhead.
[00:03:26] Samir: can you quantify expected p95 numbers? we need a ballpark for us-east with Dedicated vs Hosted for a 40-token streaming reply on an Llama-2 style 70b variant (quantized).
[00:03:38] Diego: ballpark: Hosted (shared) you might see p95 around 250-600ms depending on noisy neighbors; Dedicated with 1-2 pinned GPUs and tuned batch policy we commonly hit 180-300ms p95 for short streaming responses. Private on-prem can be lower but depends on your hardware and network — if you have A100xTB or H100 configs, you can get below 150-200ms in ideal setups.
[00:04:01] Tom: when you say batch policy, does that impact streaming latency? our UX needs first token as fast as possible.
[00:04:07] Diego: yes — batching trades throughput for latency. for streaming first token, we use micro-batching and prefix KV cache so you can get <100ms first-token in some setups, but p95 for full partial response is more like 150-300ms depending on model size.
[00:04:21] Priya: what's the token/sec capacity per GPU roughly? we saw some benchmarks with 70b quantized doing ~6-9k tokens/sec on certain GPUs.
[00:04:29] Diego: depends on hardware and quantization. on H100 you might see up to 12-18k tokens/sec sustained for generation heavy workloads on a single instance for medium tokens; A100s are lower. With Redwood's batching and continuous kv management, you'll get better aggregated throughput. but sustained vs peak is important — we size for steady-state with headroom for short bursts.
[00:04:46] Lena: for planning, assume sustained of 8k tokens/sec and peaks up to 16k for 1-2 minutes. does that map to roughly N GPUs?
[00:04:53] Diego: rough rule: for 70b quantized on H100-like hardware, 1 GPU might handle 8-10k tokens/sec sustained; for heavy interactive workloads we recommend planning 1 GPU per ~60-80 concurrent short streams depending on token lengths. so for 120 concurrent streams, you're in the 2-3 GPU range if short responses; longer summaries push that up.
[00:05:16] Tom: that seems small — can you explain the math a bit?
[00:05:19] Diego: sure — it's simplified; actual depends on seqlen, kv reuse, and parallelism. we'll provide a sizing worksheet.
[00:05:25] Maya: (interruption) i'll drop a sizing template. diego will populate a rough dedicated config for your profile.
[00:05:31] Mark: how do you handle data residency and encryption at rest for Private? we have PHI so we need HSM-backed KMS and audit trails.
[00:05:39] Diego: Private supports customer KMS/HSM and we ship audit logs to your SIEM. Dedicated also has options for customer-managed keys; hosted has encryption at rest but managed KMS by default — we can discuss BYOK for hosted in enterprise agreements.
[00:05:55] Lena: benchmarks — would you run an initial hosted benchmark with our prompt set?
[00:06:00] Maya: yes, if you can share a redacted prompt set (Priya), we can run a hosted run and give p50/p95 numbers and token/sec observations.
[00:06:07] Priya: we'll scrub PHI and share sample prompts and a couple of long-doc samples by 10/20.
[00:06:12] Diego: perfect. also we'll include a small synthetic load script for spike testing.
[00:06:17] Samir: we want to know how Redwood handles graceful degradation during capacity constraints — do you fallback to a smaller model automatically?
[00:06:24] Diego: yes — smart routing and automatic fallback policies can route to cheaper model variants or burst to other pools/regions. you can configure canary policies and automatic fallback in the Console.
[00:06:35] Kelsey: what's the typical cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated? order of magnitude?
[00:06:39] Maya: depends on committed usage. hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is higher upfront but lower per-token unit cost and predictable. we'll share a sample pricing sheet.
[00:06:48] Priya: any caveats on streaming tokens? we want partials every 50ms ideally to make the UI feel instant.
[00:06:54] Diego: sub-100ms partials are tough consistently at p95 on larger models. for small tokens and well-cached prefixes you can get snappy partials; otherwise micro-batching and low-latency kernels help. we suggested measuring first-token latency separately and optimizing for that.
[00:07:10] Lena: ok. what's next on timelines? we want a pilot in November if benchmarks look good.
[00:07:15] Maya: sounds feasible. next steps: Quasar provides prompt set by 10/20; Redwood runs hosted benchmark and returns numbers by 10/25; SE deep-dive on infra/security week of 10/26.
[00:07:26] Mark: please send SOC2, KMS, and the network diagram requirements.
[00:07:31] Diego: will do, i'll send links and a checklist.
[00:07:34] Tom: one more — what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[00:07:37] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA options depending on contract tier; typical is 99.9% uptime with latency objectives baked into the sizing. we'll include specifics in the pricing pack.
[00:07:47] Priya: for the benchmarking, do you need exact prod data or synthetic is ok?
[00:07:52] Diego: redacted real prompts + synthetic load that simulates token length distribution is best.
[00:07:57] Kelsey: anything else we should know before pilot?
[00:07:59] Maya: think about success criteria — is it strictly p95 latency or also cost per 1k tokens and UX quality? define 2-3 KPIs for pilot.
[00:08:08] Lena: primary is p95 < 300ms for chat; secondary cost per active user under $X (internal).
[00:08:13] Maya: great. i'll summarize next steps in the follow-up email.

[00:08:25] -- background chatter, some crosstalk --

[00:08:45] Diego: quick note on kernels and quantization — we recommend quantized weights for Dedicated for cost efficiency; but quantization sometimes increases latency variability; we can test a couple of quant profiles.
[00:09:05] Priya: do you support RAG workflows + retrieval latency concerns?
[00:09:09] Diego: yes — retrieval latency is additive. we recommend pre-fetching and embedding caches alongside prefix caching to keep end-to-end p95 low.
[00:09:20] Samir: what logging/tracing do we get to correlate user request to model invocation?
[00:09:25] Diego: Redwood Console provides per-request traces, token-level cost, model and route breakdowns and you can export traces to your tracing system.
[00:09:34] Mark: are there any gotchas for on-prem? network setup?
[00:09:38] Diego: on-prem requires some network peering and port openings, and KMS/HSM setup. we'll give a checklist; we also provide an appliance package in some cases.
[00:09:47] Lena: that's it from us. thanks.
[00:09:50] Maya: thanks all, follow-up email w/ attachments and links.
[00:09:55] -- meeting ends, recording stops --

Notes about transcript quality: some product names were slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "Reedwood"), and acronyms like HSM and KMS occasionally mistranscribed in the auto-caption. There were a couple of instances of speaker overlap and short crosstalk.
